meta.title: ROTA — Refine our timeless analog
meta.description: ROTA is a design-led analog photography brand. Precise tools for the chemistry half of the craft — the R1 rotary processor and the ROTA Link companion app.
meta.ogDescription: Thoughtfully designed tools for the enduring art of analog photography.

origin.title: Everything moves in circles.
origin.lede: From the roll of film to the rotation of a reel, circles are woven into the language of analog photography.
origin.body: ROTA takes its name from rotation. Not a shape borrowed for a logo — the movement the equipment actually makes: film wound into a spiral, light bent to a point, chemistry kept in motion so that it reaches the emulsion evenly.
origin.i1t: A roll is a spiral before it is an image.
origin.i1alt: A 35 mm film cartridge lying on a pale surface
origin.i2t: Light is turned in circles until it meets the plane.
origin.i2alt: The front element of a camera lens, ring within ring
origin.i3t: Chemistry reaches the emulsion by turning, not by shaking.
origin.i3alt: Film lifting out of a developing tank in a spiral
origin.note: Rotation, in this trade, is not ornament. It is the mechanism.

refine.title: Not reinvented. Refined.
refine.lede: We believe the best innovations don't erase tradition. They make it easier to experience, appreciate, and carry forward.
refine.leftBody: The process that already works: developer, stop, fix, wash. Temperatures and dilutions learned by hand, and worth keeping exactly as they are.
refine.rightBody: The same process, held steady. Rotation that does not drift, temperature that does not wander, a timer you do not have to watch.
refine.capLeft: Tradition — the practice ROTA is built around.
refine.capRight: Refined — held to the numbers the chemistry expects.
refine.p1d: Mechanism, tolerance and control: the parts that work without being seen.
refine.p2d: Fewer decisions on a screen, and clearer ones. Nothing on the machine that does not earn its place.
refine.p3d: A practice worth keeping — not a format to preserve in a museum.

process.title: More than the final image.
process.lede: The experience lives in the process — in the details, the rituals, and the satisfaction of making something by hand.
process.s1d: Film onto the reel, in the dark, by feel.
process.s2d: Time, temperature and rotation, held constant.

think.title: Understanding the whole. Building the details.
think.p1: With a background in electronics and a strong interest in how things work, I tend to approach projects as complete systems rather than isolated parts.
think.p2: I enjoy breaking down complex problems, understanding how different elements connect, and working through the process of turning an idea into something tangible.
think.p3: For me, the most rewarding part is not simply solving one technical problem, but understanding how everything comes together in the final product.

why.title: Refine our timeless analog.
why.p1: ROTA began with a simple interest in analog photography and the tools behind the process.
why.p2: Rather than reinventing a traditional craft, I wanted to explore how thoughtful design and modern technology could make its tools more precise, intuitive, and enjoyable to use.
why.p3: ROTA is an ongoing personal project built around that idea — bringing together engineering, product thinking, and a lasting appreciation for analog photography.

close.title: Refine our timeless analog.
close.lede: A personal project, shaped by curiosity and the process of making.

hero.lede: Precision rotary processing for film. Controlled rotation, precise temperature, reproducible results — from development to final rinse.

intro.title: Consistent processing, run after run
intro.body1: ROTA R1 is a rotary film roller processor built around one principle: once a recipe is set, every step is executed the same way, every time. Rotation speed, direction changes, temperature and timing are handled by the machine — not by hand.
intro.body2: Recipes are managed on the device or synced from the ROTA Link companion app over Bluetooth LE and Wi-Fi. Firmware updates arrive over the air, so the machine improves without opening the case.
intro.f1d: Adjustable drum speed with smooth acceleration and reversal, so chemistry distributes evenly across the emulsion.
intro.f2d: A PT1000 RTD sensor and closed-loop control hold the bath within the range your chemistry expects.
intro.f3d: Store multi-step recipes — developer, stop, fix, wash — with per-step time, temperature and agitation.

install.title: Installing firmware
install.warn: Do not power off the machine during an update. If an update is interrupted, the previous firmware is restored automatically.
install.s1d: Get the latest firmware package from the Firmware section above, or from the GitHub releases page.
install.s2d: Install directly over the air when the machine is online, or use the ROTA Link app to start an update over Bluetooth.
install.s3d: The bootloader verifies the staged image, writes the OTA metadata, and copies it on the next boot. Progress is shown on the device display.
install.s4d: After the reboot, check the firmware version on the device under Settings — it should match the release you installed.

about.title: Built for the darkroom
about.body: ROTA is an independent hardware project for analog photographers: a film roller processor designed to make consistent, repeatable development part of everyday practice. The ROTA Link app and this site are part of the same effort — everything around the machine should be as considered as the machine itself.

meta.title: ROTA Link — Film Processing Timer & Companion App
meta.description: A considered companion for analog photography. Recipes, a timer that warns in three degrees, a notification that keeps the run alive, and a film log you can export as an image.
meta.ogTitle: ROTA Link — Film Processing Timer & Companion App
meta.ogDescription: Recipes, timing and device state on one quiet screen — plus a film log that leaves the phone as a finished card.

hero.tagline: A more considered way to process film.
hero.lede: A precise, intuitive companion for your film processing workflow.

timer.title: Everything you need. Nothing in the way.
timer.body: The app opens on the timer because the timer is the point: the step you are in, the time left, the recipe behind it, and what comes next — legible at arm's length, with wet hands. Turn the phone and the same run becomes an instrument: one number that fills the screen, a bar that closes behind you, and the next three steps laid out where a thumb can reach them.
timer.f1d: Step, countdown, whole-process progress and next stage share the first view. The controls never leave the bottom of the screen.
timer.f2d: Every step carries its own duration. Temperature and rotation belong to the recipe, because that is how the controller stores them.
timer.f3d: A standalone darkroom timer with your own recipes on board. No account, no pairing, no machine required.
timer.detail1v: Jost Light, tabular figures — digits never shift as the time changes.
timer.detail2v: Finished steps tick, the running step turns brass, the rest stay quiet.
timer.holdNote: SKIP is a two-second hold — the wait is the undo.

remind.title: Three degrees of warning, none of them an alarm.
remind.body: The processor has always counted down in three steps — a warm light when a step is nearly done, a quicker flash for the last five seconds, then a steady red once the time is spent. The app keeps that language instead of borrowing a phone alarm: the same three degrees, the same brass, the same beeps.
remind.l1v: Ten seconds left. The digits breathe, one slow pass every 1.5 s, and never go fully dark.
remind.l2v: Five seconds left. The digits flash every 650 ms, and each flash carries one short click.
remind.l3v: The time is spent. The colour holds steady — a red that stays lit reads calmer than a red that blinks.
remind.soundNote: Each pattern is a copy of the firmware buzzer — same pitch, same rhythm — so a step sounds the same in your hand as it does on the machine. The ruler is 1.6 seconds.
remind.soundFoot: Silent while a step is paused, and off in one tap from the landscape view — darkrooms have neighbours. Volume follows the media channel, not notifications.

notif.title: The run continues after you put the phone down.
notif.body: A foreground service holds the timer while you are doing something else, and posts one quiet card. It never rings: the beeps are the app's own voice, and a notification with a sound of its own would say everything twice. Collapsed it carries four readings; expanded it adds the next three steps, and three actions that work without opening the app.
notif.collapsedV: Recipe, step, countdown, stage progress. Everything else waits.
notif.expandedV: Elapsed against stage length, the next three steps, and a status line that only takes colour when it has something to say.
notif.f1d: The channel is low-importance: no sound, no vibration, no badge. While the run is live the card cannot be swiped away; when the process ends it dismisses itself.
notif.f2d: Pause, skip and end are system actions, so the label always matches the tap — "Next" while a step is overrunning, "Restart" at the end of the process.
notif.f3d: The card is a custom layout. When a ROM refuses to inflate it, the app falls back to the standard template with the title, text, progress and all three actions still there.
notif.f4d: The card paints no background: the shade owns the material and the rounding. All the app adds is ink that follows the system theme — #1B1B1B on light, #F2F2EC on dark — one brass progress line, and three semantic colours for ending soon, overtime and complete.

recipes.title: Your process. Your precision.
recipes.body: Five processes ship with the machine — C-41, ECN-2, E-6, black-and-white negative and black-and-white reversal — and five slots are yours to define. A recipe is a sequence of steps with a duration each, plus one temperature and one rotation speed for the whole run.
recipes.aside: Built-in slots keep the machine's names. Custom slots are yours, and can be edited, reordered and deleted on the phone.
recipes.editorCaption: Recipe editor — drag to reorder, durations as MM:SS
recipes.listCaption: Recipes — five built-in slots, five of your own
recipes.c41: Colour negative, one temperature for the whole run.
recipes.ecn2: Cinema negative, with a dedicated rem-jet removal step.
recipes.e6: Transparency, eight steps from first developer to stabilizer.
recipes.bw: Classic negative at 20 °C, five steps including pre-soak.
recipes.bwr: Reversal black and white: first developer, bleach, re-develop.
recipes.custom: A slot of your own — push processing, odd dilutions, house rules.
recipes.editorBody: A custom recipe is the same object as a built-in one: a name, a note, one temperature, one rotation speed and up to thirteen steps. Durations are entered as MM:SS, steps reorder by dragging, and a deleted step closes the gap without a jump.
recipes.editorNote: Recipes can be read from and written to the machine over Bluetooth — one slot at a time, whichever slot you choose.

workflow.title: A clearer view of every step.
workflow.body: You should always know three things: what is running, what comes next, and how much is left. The running step is brass, finished steps are ticked, everything else stays out of the way.

film.title: A roll, written down while you still remember it.
film.body: Film Log is a card you fill in as you go: the stock, the frames, the process that made them, the sentence you will want in six months. It exports as a single PNG at 1080 px, drawn from the same measurements as the card on screen — so the file is the card, not a screenshot of it.
film.c1n: Two cities, one roll, mostly strangers. Scanned at home, nothing pushed.
film.c1p: Portraits pair up two to a row; each 3:2 landscape then takes the full width on its own.
film.c2t: The light went before the film did.
film.c2n: One evening on the same headland: the sea going flat, the city switching its lights on behind the pines. Six frames that held still.
film.c2p: 6×7 is 1.225 : 1, close enough to square that a landscape and a portrait share a row — twice — and two portraits close it.
film.c3n: Nothing cropped: the edge markings and the sprocket holes stay, so the roll is still in the picture. A week of the same street at noon.
film.c3p: Full-frame scans come out almost square, so each one takes a row of its own — no pairing possible, none needed.
film.f1v: One line, seventy characters, up to two lines of type.
film.f2v: Stock, format and ISO on one line, with the cassette mark at the start.
film.f3v: Body and lens — optional. Left empty, the row is simply not printed.
film.f4v: Up to 36, each at its own ratio. Portraits pair up; a landscape takes the full width.
film.f5v: Recipe, temperature and every step with its time. Switch it off for rolls sent to a lab.
film.f6v: 220 characters of what you would otherwise forget, and a roll number in the footer.
film.g1d: The PNG is re-rendered at the same proportions as the card on screen, so edit boxes, drag highlights and the add-cell never appear in the file.
film.g2d: Nothing is cropped or padded to a fixed ratio. A four-frame card is short; a thirty-six-frame card is long.
film.g3d: Written to Pictures/ROTA through MediaStore on Android 10 and later — no storage permission — then handed to the system share sheet.

connected.title: Connected when you need it. Independent when you don't.
connected.body: Connecting the machine changes what the app can show, never what it can do. The timer behaves identically on both sides of this page.
connected.leftBody: No device, no pairing. Timing, recipes and steps behave exactly as they do with the machine switched on.
connected.leftB1: Starts on the timer and stays there
connected.leftB3: No account, no network, no extra permissions
connected.rightBody: The same screen, with the machine's own state beside it.
connected.rightB2: Target temperature and rotation, read from the recipe
connected.rightB3: Bath temperature, actual rpm and direction — once the device link reports them
connected.honest: Live telemetry is not reported by the current device-link protocol, so bath temperature, actual rotation speed and direction stay blank rather than showing a made-up value. What you see above is the app's real connected state.

analog.title: Film is not a thing of the past.
analog.body: Digital tools did not replace the darkroom. They made it easier to repeat. ROTA Link takes over the part of the process a person is worst at — counting — and leaves the part that matters, judgement, to you.
analog.caption: Silver, gelatin, and a clock that behaves.
